mbm-0693.clue: I sing my part into the wardrobe.
mbm-0693.quote: My room echoes so much I can't hear the ends of my notes. I open the wardrobe and sing to three coats and a scarf. They have made me an unexpectedly precise tenor.

mbm-0694.clue: I like the club's upstairs landing.
mbm-0694.quote: From the landing I can watch a whole floor find the beat at different times. Last week the woman collecting glasses was the first to catch the change. We followed her back down.

mbm-0695.clue: I put a tide line around my vase.
mbm-0695.quote: I dipped it in two blue glazes, one over the other. Where they met, the kiln left a thin green foam. My aunt turned the vase twice before realizing the water couldn't move.

mbm-0696.clue: I birdwatch from the bike rack.
mbm-0696.quote: A wagtail works the puddles outside our library. From the bench I only see its back. Between two bicycle wheels I get a front-row view of that ridiculous little dance.

mbm-0697.clue: I juggle to the crossing bell.
mbm-0697.quote: I used to practice three clubs in the yard by the tracks. When a train went past, the bell gave me my beat. At my first show a tram rang outside and my hands knew exactly when to start.

mbm-0698.clue: I play son for the kitchen door.
mbm-0698.quote: It swings on a spring. When we rehearse in the courtyard I can tell which songs the cooks like by how long someone holds it open. Our last chorus kept the whole kitchen out there.

mbm-0699.clue: I coded a clock with a hungry face.
mbm-0699.quote: Every hour a pixel mouth eats one more slice of pie. I meant it as a joke for our kitchen computer. Mum called me at noon to report that my clock had finished lunch.

mbm-0700.clue: I read a chapter by each window.
mbm-0700.quote: Our train carriage has a seat that catches the morning sun. When the train turns, I move my book across the aisle. The conductor says I'm the only passenger orbiting a novel.

mbm-0701.clue: I took the bridge out of my putt.
mbm-0701.quote: The mini-golf bridge was under repair and they sent us along the side. My little cousin banked a perfect shot off the rail. The repairman put down his brush and clapped with us.

mbm-0702.clue: I wave after I drop the handle.
mbm-0702.quote: My first clean water-ski run ended with both hands in the air before I remembered to let go. Now I wait till the skis settle, then wave back to the boat. My friend always waves twice.

mbm-0703.quote: My little cousin calls out ice cream flavors instead of numbers. By pistachio I'm usually concentrating hard. We once made it all the way to a flavor she had to invent.

mbm-0704.clue: I keep the first captured stone.
mbm-0704.quote: Dad taught me baduk on a board with one corner bleached by the sun. The first black stone I ever captured lives in my pocket. We count it back into the bowl before every game.

mbm-0705.clue: I hike to a tree with a window.
mbm-0705.quote: Two limbs grew back together and made a frame for the far ridge. I've taken the same picture there in four seasons. Winter has the best mountains. Summer has the best bugs.

mbm-0706.clue: I give one puppet a wooden eyebrow.
mbm-0706.quote: It tips down on a thread when the old judge gets suspicious. One afternoon the thread stuck and he looked furious at a cabbage for the entire play. The children demanded another cabbage scene.

mbm-0707.clue: I run home by the red doors.
mbm-0707.quote: Our town has six red doors on one winding loop. On dark mornings I count them to keep going. The bakery repainted theirs blue and nearly sent me round for a seventh.

mbm-0708.clue: I fold my bookmarks into little chairs.
mbm-0708.quote: It's a trick I learned from a book of paper models. When I stop reading, a tiny paper chair waits beside the last line. Last week somebody made my chair a matching paper lamp.

mbm-0709.clue: I shop by the sound of a saucer.
mbm-0709.quote: I wanted a mismatched tea set that still sounded like a set. The market seller let me tap each saucer with my fingernail. She found the last one for me without looking up.

mbm-0710.clue: I kayak past a letterbox for ducks.
mbm-0710.quote: It's really a nesting box on stilts. My nephew calls it the duck post office. I paddle by in spring and report how many customers are waiting on the roof.

mbm-0711.clue: I rehearse the scene behind the curtain.
mbm-0711.quote: As a stagehand I knew everybody's entrances by heart. Then an actor got sick and I had to step through the curtain myself. I'd practiced every line except my own name at the curtain call.

mbm-0712.clue: I visit the last stop on the tram.
mbm-0712.quote: That's where you find out who the tram is really for. One line ended by a little public garden. By the return trip I had learned the names of three roses from a man with a watering can.

mbm-0713.clue: I bring a spare hiking hat for lunch.
mbm-0713.quote: My usual lunch rock is sunny. I lay the spare hat over the cheese while I eat my bread. My hiking partner only stopped teasing me after she tasted her own melted sandwich.

mbm-0714.clue: I climb until I see the kite.
mbm-0714.quote: At our gym one roof beam has a kite caught on it. From the ground it's just a red scrap. From the top hold I can see its painted eyes. I wave to them every time.

mbm-0715.clue: I lay out my quilt on the stairs.
mbm-0715.quote: The landing is too narrow for the whole thing. I drape the rows down one stair at a time. My nephew greeted the last one like a waterfall and put a toy boat at the bottom.

mbm-0716.clue: I wrote the world's smallest ticket booth.
mbm-0716.quote: My niece's toy train needed fares. I made a program that issues a different colored ticket every time she taps the key. She charges one button to ride and I'm almost out of buttons.

mbm-0717.clue: I owe my waltz to a dropped earring.
mbm-0717.quote: My partner spotted her earring on the floor without breaking step. We circled it for the whole last verse, then bowed and picked it up. Our teacher called it exceptionally attentive floorcraft.
